title: Price-snapshot store coverage and provenance defects
rule: A snapshot is published only where the publisher prints a number. Missing fields are null and counted here; none is derived.

temporal_coverage.finding: The only file that evidences an opening number covers 2021-2021; the only file that evidences a closing number covers 2006-2018. They never overlap, so 0 markets have both an opening and a closing number from a single publisher. No opening-to-closing move can be measured from this upstream.

defects.claim: Two nflverse files disagree about the closing spread for the same game.
defects.measure: 1101 of 3368 games (32.7%) where closing_lines.csv (home side) and games.csv spread_line differ, after normalising the documented sign convention.
defects.consequence: Only one of them can be the closing number. Until the publisher says which, neither is used as the model's benchmark for CLV; both are stored and labelled.
defects.how_to_close: Ask nflverse which source backfills games.csv lines, or price a licensed feed and drop the nflverse lines from the benchmark.

defects.claim: initial_lines.csv is not the opening line for the games it lists.
defects.measure: 510 of 544 2021 spreads (93.8%) are inconsistent with games.csv spread_line for the same game.
defects.consequence: Treating this file as 'the opening line' would mislabel a number by more than a touchdown on some games. It is stored as `initial_lines` evidence only, not as an opening price.
defects.how_to_close: A feed that timestamps every snapshot (see Q-P2).

defects.claim: closing_lines.csv prints a price on fewer than half of its rows.
defects.measure: 8850 of 20490 rows carry an American price (43.2%), and only 505 games have a closing SPREAD price (2017-2018 only).
defects.consequence: EV and ROI can only be computed on the priced subset; every backtest states its priced n, not its total n.
defects.how_to_close: Licensed price feed, or a documented capture of one book's closing numbers.

defects.claim: No closing line row in the usable upstream names a book.
defects.measure: The closing snapshot names a book on 0 of 20336 store rows. The only rows that name a book at all are 544, and those name a three-letter vendor code (WSGT) rather than a market or a full book name.
defects.consequence: A model price can be compared with a market price only if both refer to the same market. Without a book, 'the market line' is an unnamed composite, so beat-the-close numbers are not published from it.
defects.how_to_close: Record the book with every snapshot (Q-P1).

defects.claim: No line row in the usable upstream carries a timestamp.
defects.measure: 0 of 20336 store rows have a timestamp on either snapshot. The publisher's own files have no time column at all.
defects.consequence: 'Opening' and 'closing' are inferences from a file name and row order, not recordings. Any CLV built on them is a proxy, and is labelled as such.

ready_for.explanation: The store can support a fair-line vs market-line column for the markets that are complete. It cannot support true CLV (no timestamp, no book) and can support ROI only on the priced subset.

games.spread_line.definition: The spread line for the game. A positive number means the home team was favored by that many points, a negative number means the away team was favored by that many points. (DATASETS.md, line 109.)

games.total_line.definition: The total line for the game. (DATASETS.md, line 110.)

games.home_moneyline.definition: American odds on the home team's moneyline. No definition is printed in DATASETS.md; the column is used on the strength of its name only, which is why every row built from it is flagged.

games.away_moneyline.definition: American odds on the away team's moneyline. No definition is printed in DATASETS.md; used on the strength of its name only.

initial_lines.line.definition: A spread or total on game `about` at sportsbook code `sportsbook`. The file name says 'initial'; the publisher prints no definition and no timestamp.

closing_lines.line.definition: A line on game `alt_game_id` for `type` in {SPREAD, TOTAL, MONEYLINE}. The file name says 'closing'; no book, no retrieval timestamp and no definition are printed.

_how_to_close.book: Record the book on every price row. nflverse does not print one for games.csv or closing_lines.csv; a licensed feed (or a documented manual capture) does. Until then no row can say which market it is.
_how_to_close.timestamp: Capture a timestamp with every snapshot. An opening number without a time is only an opening number because a file is named 'initial'.
_how_to_close.prices: Every price the model needs must be a published price. Today only 505 games have a closing spread price, and no game has an opening price.
